chunks: And it was narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, who said:

Al-Marzubān asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the slaughtered animal of one born of zina, while they had known him to be such. He said: “There is no harm in it, and the woman and the child, if they are compelled to it.”

key_terms.اضْطُرُّوا: they were compelled or driven by necessity
key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: the child or minor, mentioned here in relation to necessity
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman, mentioned here in relation to slaughter and necessity
key_terms.ذَبِيحَةِ: the slaughtered animal or slaughtered meat under discussion
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is unobjectionable
key_terms.وَلَدِ الزِّنَا: a person born out of wedlock

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the slaughtered animal of someone born out of wedlock in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the slaughter of an animal by a person known to be born out of wedlock. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no harm in it, and also mentions the case of a woman and a child when necessity compels them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4178 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated that

Al-Marzuban asked Abu al-Hasan (as) about the slaughtered animal of a child born out of wedlock, and they were certain of his status.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it, and it is permissible for a woman and a child if they are in necessity."
